articles.title: ‘A life changing blow’: Malaysian Commonwealth Games champion loses right arm after motorcycle crash
articles.summary: Malaysian weightlifter Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin has lost his right arm after a serious motorcycle crash in Kuala Lumpur.
articles.body: Malaysian weightlifter Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin has lost his right arm after a serious motorcycle crash in Kuala Lumpur. The 2026 Commonwealth Games gold medallist underwent an operation lasting about seven hours at Kuala Lumpur Hospital on November 17. Doctors amputated his arm above the elbow after efforts to save it failed. Three days after the accident, Hafizuddin was currently awake and in a stable condition, according to Malaysian Weightlifting Federation president Ayub Rahmat. The news has shocked Malaysia’s sporting community, but officials say they will support him through treatment and help him plan his future.Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin Loses Right Arm After Seven-Hour Surgery Following Motorcycle AccidentHafizuddin was riding along the Sungai Besi-Ulu Kelang Elevated Expressway, known as the SUKE Highway, at around 11pm on November 16. He was travelling from Ampang towards Bukit Jalil when he reportedly lost control of his motorcycle.The National Sports Council said he suffered injuries to his legs, shoulder and head. Doctors also found a collection of blood near his right shoulder. He was taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital, where he received urgent medical care.The most serious damage was to his right arm. It had broken bones and severe injuries to the blood vessels. Doctors first tried to save the limb during the long operation. However, they later decided that removing it above the elbow was necessary to protect his life.Malaysian Weightlifting Federation president Ayub Rahmat confirmed the operation and later gave an update on Hafizuddin’s condition. Speaking to AFP on November 19, Ayub said: "He is awake and smiling." He added that the athlete’s physical condition was improving, although the accident had changed his future.The Malaysian government has said it will cover the cost of Hafizuddin’s treatment and medical care. The support will also include follow-up care and hospital accommodation until he is discharged. His training allowance is set to continue at its current rate, according to Youth and Sports Minister Taufiq Johari.The National Sports Council is also expected to help with his recovery. Officials have said that support for the athlete and his family remains a priority.Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin's 2026 Commonwealth Games Gold Medal and Future in WeightliftingThe crash came only a few months after Hafizuddin reached the biggest milestone of his career. He won the men’s 88kg weightlifting gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland, in July.He lifted a total of 345kg to take the title. His result included a 162kg snatch and a 183kg clean and jerk. The snatch also set a Malaysian national record and a Commonwealth Games record.That win made Hafizuddin one of Malaysia’s leading young weightlifters and put him on the radar ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. His loss of an arm means he is no longer expected to continue as a competitive weightlifter.However, the Malaysian Weightlifting Federation is looking at ways to keep him connected to the sport. Ayub said the federation was considering a future role for him in coaching, potentially at state level in Perlis, where Hafizuddin is from.The federation has also spoken about providing support as he adjusts to life after the accident. The focus now is on his medical care and recovery, while officials work out what kind of role may be possible for him later.Hafizuddin’s case has also drawn support from Malaysia’s sports leadership. Youth and Sports Minister Taufiq Johari visited him in hospital, while national sports bodies have promised help for his treatment and longer-term needs. His family has asked for privacy as he recovers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Anthony Joshua shares extreme daily diet and water intake as Tyson Fury fight gets closer
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua is taking his preparation seriously ahead of his December 11 showdown with Tyson Fury in Cardiff.
articles.body: Anthony Joshua is taking his preparation seriously ahead of his December 11 showdown with Tyson Fury in Cardiff. The former heavyweight champion has revealed that his training camp involves eating between 4,000 and 4,500 calories every day and drinking around 10 litres of water. While his food intake is already far above what most people need, Joshua says staying hydrated is an even bigger part of his daily routine. The 37-year-old also opened up about his possible retirement and what he wants to do after leaving boxing.Anthony Joshua Explains His 4,500-Calorie Diet and 10-Litre Water Routine Ahead of Tyson Fury FightThe long-awaited meeting between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury is finally getting closer. The British rivals will meet at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11, ending years of talk about a fight that boxing fans have wanted to see.With the date approaching, Joshua is putting extra attention into his body and training. The 6ft 6in heavyweight recently spoke to The Sun's Clemmie Moodie about the amount of food and water he needs during fight camp.Joshua revealed that he eats between 4,000 and 4,500 calories every day while preparing for a fight. That is a huge amount of food, but his training demands a lot of energy. As a heavyweight boxer, he needs to maintain his strength while keeping up with long and demanding training sessions.However, food is not the only thing he watches closely. Joshua explained that drinking enough water takes even more attention during his preparation."People talk about how many calories they eat. The thing is, is how many litres of water we have to drink. I think I go for about 10 litres of water a day," he told The Sun.His daily water intake caught Moodie's attention during the conversation. She asked whether drinking so much water meant he had to visit the bathroom throughout the day and wake up during the night.Joshua admitted that managing the amount of water he drinks is not always simple. He also explained how he handles it before going to sleep."You have to stagger the way you drink the water before bed, like 500 millilitres, a litre here, then another 500," he said.His routine is built around the needs of his training camp. However, his water intake should not be treated as a target for everyone, as hydration needs can vary from person to person.Anthony Joshua Opens Up About Retirement and His Plans After BoxingWhile the Tyson Fury fight remains his main focus, Joshua also spoke about life after boxing. The former two-time unified heavyweight champion admitted that he is starting to think more seriously about retirement.He explained that his approach to the sport has always been about discipline rather than enjoying every part of the lifestyle that comes with being a famous boxer."That's the motto I have with boxing. Boxing is not glamorous," Joshua said."I keep it pretty simple, straightforward. I do what I can. I live by what I need, not by what I want. And it's working out."Joshua also shared an idea about what he might do once his boxing career comes to an end. He mentioned investing in Under Armour and possibly becoming a shareholder in the sportswear company."And then I think when I finish fighting, I'll be more chilled and then maybe I can go and look at investing in Under Armour stocks or maybe have a share in the Under Armour company or something like that. But as for now, I'm pretty content," he added.The British boxer also spoke about his age and admitted that retirement may not be too far away."I can't believe I'm 37. It's crazy. So when am I going to retire? I think, yes, pretty soon. I'm getting old now," he said.He later added: "From an athlete's point of view, I'm getting old."Joshua made it clear that he does not believe he has many years left in the sport."So maybe that will be our next sit down when we talk about plans for after boxing, because that will be coming around pretty soon. I haven't got many years ahead of me," he said.For now, his attention remains on December 11. The fight against Tyson Fury could become one of the biggest nights of Joshua's career, while his comments suggest he is also thinking about what comes next.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 2026 Grand Slam of Darts: Draw, schedule, groups, prize money and format explained
articles.summary: One of the most exciting majors of the year is almost here!
articles.body:
The revamped Grand Slam of Darts begins this month, with 48 players competing for one of the sport's most coveted titles.

The event has some key changes, so it's important to know the details before watching the action unfold.

What to know about the Grand Slam of Darts

Let's take a look at some of the specifics of the tournament.

2026 Grand Slam of Darts Draw/group stage

Here are 16 different groups for the group stage.

*The table leader after the round-robin stage is completed will advance to the last 16

Nathan Aspinall vs. Maik Kuivenhoven (P)

*Matches played between Saturday afternoon's losing players and players from the group who haven't played yet

Luke Woodhouse vs. Krzysztof Ratajski (J)

*Matches played between Saturday evening's losing players and players from the group who haven't played yet

*Matches played between Saturday's winning player and the player who played their first match of the event on Sunday (Groups A-H)

*Matches played between Saturday's winning player and the player who played their first match of the event on Sunday (Groups I-P)

Gabriel Clemens vs. Rusty-Jake Rodriguez (O)

Michael van Gerwen vs. Jeffrey de Graaf (L)

Here is the bracket for the event after the group stage.

The Grand Slam of Darts is a 48-player tournament (16 more players than 2025), with various qualification routes to get there.

The seeded players consist of the top-16 players, who are each assigned to a separate group, and then have two additional players assigned to their group in the event's draw (one player from pool #2 and #3, with #2 having higher-ranked qualifiers than #3).

The first four days of the tournament (Nov. 14 - 17) will be purely group stage games, as each player will play the other two players in their group (round-robin format). These games will be played to best-of-9 legs.

The winner of each group will advance to the last 16. If there were to be a three-player tie, it would be determined by leg difference and then legs won, legs won against throw, tournament average and lastly a nine-dart shootout.

The knockout stage (last 16) will begin on Nov. 18. The first round of the knockout stage is played to best-of-19 legs.

The final three rounds (quarterfinals, semifinals & final) of the tournament will take place from Nov. 18 - 22 and will all be played to best-of-31 legs.

articles.title: Why is Zac Taylor so excited Paycor is hosting Elder-Princeton?
articles.summary: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said he's thrilled that Elder and Princeton are playing their high school playoff regional final game at Paycor Stadium.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said he's thrilled that Elder and Princeton are playing their high school playoff regional final game at Paycor Stadium on Friday.

"I love it," Taylor said. "I mean, I really do love it. I'll be following the game. We'll be working since our week's a little different. So I'll get to hear the environment out there and maybe poke my head out. But two programs that have had great years. I've watched them both over the course of the season."

"So it should be a great game," Taylor continued. "It's awesome that they're doing it here at Paycor. I think that's a really cool experience for those kids. (I) went to the game last year when it was St. X and Elder and watched a lot of high school football this year."

The Bengals take on the Steelers with a white out Sunday evening

"I'm not always at the games, but I'm certainly watching on streams and following on Twitter to see what the scores are," Taylor added. "And a lot of programs that I like to follow as I've gotten to know some coaches. So the Elder-Princeton game's going to be a great game."

The day after the Bengals' rout of Pittsburgh on " Sunday Night Football ," Taylor talked about how impressed he was with right tackle Amarius Mims' dominant effort against TJ Watt and the Steelers ' defense.

Taylor was asked after the game whether he heard MVP chants for Burrow from the crowd.

"Well, I mean, (it would) be impossible to say anybody's playing better than him," Taylor told reporters after the game. "I'm not watching every game, but I can promise you people that aren't talking about him aren't watching all of our games because if you are, it's really hard to say that this dude's not the best player on planet Earth."

articles.title: Vermont ousts North Florida from NCAA Tournament with 2-1 overtime win
articles.summary: The University of North Florida played Vermont on Nov. 19 in the NCAA men’s soccer tournament. Did the Ospreys survive in New England?
articles.body:
It can't get much more agonizing for the University of North Florida men's soccer team .

For the third season in a row, the Ospreys were knocked out of the NCAA Tournament in the first round by either a one-goal margin or in penalty kicks. Vermont's Jack McDowell took a crossing pass from Luis Vetter with 4:14 left in overtime and jammed the ball past UNF keeper Luciano Natolia for a sudden-death goal that gave the Catamounts a 2-1 victory on Nov. 19 at Virtue Field in Burlington, Vt.

UNF (13-5-3) fell behind 1-0 in the 34th minute on Luis Fischer's goal but tied it with 41 seconds left in the half when Ponte Vedra High graduate and senior forward Mark Romano scored off assists by senior forward Alex Monde and senior midfielder Anton Khelil .

The breakaway goal from the right side was Romano's ninth goal of the season to tie Aron Martinez of Florida Gulf Coast for the most in the ASUN and Khelil's sixth assist, moving him into a tie for third in the conference.

The two teams battled through the final 45 minutes before going to overtime. Natoli and the Ospreys held off a late barrage of Vermont shots and Cats goalkeeper Niklas Herceg saved a direct kick from 30 yards out by Khelil.

Stepan Fiker of Vermont started the game-winning play with a pass to Vetter, who crossed the ball from the left side to McDowell.

Vermont (11-2-5), an at-large team from the America East Conference, advances to a second-round game on Nov. 22 at Clemson. UNF, which won its third consecutive ASUN title for an automatic berth in the NCAA by beating Queens on Nov. 14 2-0, is still looking for its first-ever NCAA Tournament victory.

The Ospreys lost to North Carolina last year in penalty kicks, 6-5, after regulation and two overtimes ended in a 2-2 tie. UNF fell to West Virginia 2-1 in 2024 and lost to Coastal Carolina 1-0 in 2015.

articles.title: Lakers Linked to 3 Centers After Jazz Exposes Costly Weakness
articles.summary: The Lakers' loss to a depleted Jazz team exposed a troubling weakness, and three potential trade options could offer help. The post Lakers Linked to 3 Center...
articles.body:
The Lakers' nine-game winning streak ended with more than a disappointing loss. It exposed a frontcourt problem that could become increasingly difficult to ignore.

Los Angeles fell 109-97 to the Utah Jazz on Wednesday, surrendering the rebounding battle to a team missing three of its most prominent big men.

Utah played without Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkić. Yet the Jazz outrebounded the Lakers 45-42, with Mo Bamba collecting 16 rebounds.

The defeat reinforced concerns raised by Michael Duarte of the California Post, who recently identified three potential backup center options for Los Angeles: Milwaukee's Jericho Sims, former Laker Jaxson Hayes and Clippers veteran Brook Lopez.

For a Lakers team with championship ambitions, finding reliable help behind Walker Kessler could become a priority.

Lakers Outrebounded by Short-Handed Jazz

Kessler returned Wednesday after missing the Lakers' overtime victory against Charlotte because of right lower leg soreness.

He finished with 10 points and 11 rebounds, but struggled offensively, shooting 3-for-7 from the field and 4-for-10 from the free-throw line.

His backup, Sandro Mamukelashvili, endured an even tougher night.

Mamukelashvili managed six points and three rebounds in nearly 21 minutes. He missed nine of his 10 field-goal attempts, including all four shots from beyond the arc.

Kevon Looney, who started against Charlotte during Kessler's absence, did not play Wednesday because of a coach's decision.

The Lakers received little help elsewhere.

Jarred Vanderbilt grabbed five rebounds but went scoreless, while the team's offense sputtered throughout the second half.

Luka Dončić scored 29 points but shot 10-for-28 and committed nine turnovers.

Los Angeles made just nine of 33 three-point attempts and shot 38.2% overall.

Utah outscored the Lakers 31-21 in the fourth quarter, snapping their winning streak.

Brook Lopez Among Lakers' Potential Center Options

Duarte identified Lopez as an intriguing possibility because of his combination of rim protection and outside shooting.

The veteran Clippers center could give coach JJ Redick a different option when Kessler rests while providing additional spacing for Dončić.

Sims offers a more traditional interior presence.

The Milwaukee center could provide rebounding, athleticism and energy around the basket, although his limited offensive range would do little to address Los Angeles' perimeter shooting.

Hayes represents a familiar alternative.

The former Lakers center, now with Utah, finished Wednesday's game with six points, seven rebounds and two blocks against his former team.

His athleticism and familiarity with Redick's system could make a reunion worth considering.

However, Duarte's suggestions are potential fits, not confirmation that trade negotiations are underway.

Rob Pelinka Faces Important Roster Decision

The Lakers' frontcourt depth was already tested Tuesday when Kessler sat out against Charlotte.

Los Angeles survived that game behind Quentin Grimes' 47-point performance.

Wednesday's defeat showed that getting Kessler back does not automatically solve the problem.

Even against a depleted Utah frontcourt, the Lakers struggled to control the glass and received minimal offensive support from their reserve big men.

A backup center alone would not fix their shooting or turnover issues.

But for president of basketball operations Rob Pelinka, strengthening the position could provide valuable insurance as the season progresses.

The Lakers have demonstrated their potential during an impressive start.

Their loss to Utah offered a reminder that their roster still has weaknesses worth addressing.

articles.title: Bleacher Report Power Rankings: Browns land at the 14 spot
articles.summary: The Browns remain in contention in the AFC North after Week 11.
articles.body:
Last week it felt like the Cleveland Browns season was circling the drain. They had lost two games in a row and fallen out of the playoff picture. It felt inevitable that the slide would continue as they took on a very talented Houston Texans team.

However, the slide did not continue. The Browns got the win on Sunday and are back in the playoff graphic. Now they are in the driver's seat to make the postseason.

As a result, this team is moving up in the power rankings. Pundits have to give Cleveland their respect as the Browns continue to exceed expectations. This was reflected in the week eleven power rankings via Bleacher Report's Gary Davenport .

Coming into Sunday the Browns ranked 16th in these rankings. Following their win over the Texans, this group has moved up to 14th. Davenport had this to say.

"Cleveland is finding ways to win even when the odds are stacked against the team. For example, the Houston Texans led 17-0 at halftime. Once again, the Browns defense made life difficult on its opponent and provided an opportunity for the Deshaun Watson-led offense to chip away at the deficit before making big plays down the stretch."

He described the Browns as resilient in his evaluation, and it's hard to argue that. Anytime it has felt like their backs have been against the wall, this team has responded. Now they need to show that they can still keep this mindset up as a team that is becoming expected to make the postseason.

articles.title: LIVE F1 | Las Vegas GP FP2 awaits after unprecedented FP1 washout
articles.summary: Welcome to GPblog's live coverage of the second free practice session for the 2026 Formula 1 Las Vegas GP. After an extraordinary opening session in which no...
articles.body:
Welcome to GPblog's live coverage of the second free practice session for the 2026 Formula 1 Las Vegas GP. After an extraordinary opening session in which not a single driver managed to set a lap time, the teams will be hoping for considerably more running under the lights of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit. Follow all the action from FP2 right here.

Las Vegas GP weekend begins with unprecedented FP1 washout

The opening practice session in Las Vegas produced one of the most unusual scenes in recent Formula 1 history, as heavy rain prevented every driver from recording a single representative lap time.

Despite the session running its full scheduled duration, the timing screens remained empty, with Sergio Perez technically appearing at the top of the classification after venturing onto the circuit without completing a timed lap.

The extraordinary conditions left teams without any meaningful data from the opening hour, making FP2 particularly important as preparations continue for qualifying and Saturday night's Grand Prix.

With the Las Vegas Circuit featuring long straights, heavy braking zones and relatively low levels of downforce, drivers will be eager to understand how their cars perform around the challenging street layout. Tyre temperatures could also prove crucial, particularly given the cooler conditions traditionally experienced during nighttime running in Las Vegas.

Mercedes, Ferrari and Red Bull prepare for crucial FP2 session

Mercedes enter the weekend with plenty of attention surrounding their performance, having introduced four aerodynamic updates specifically designed to improve efficiency around the Las Vegas circuit.

Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull have also brought modifications as teams look to maximise their competitiveness on one of the fastest street circuits on the calendar.

The championship battle adds another layer of intrigue to the weekend, with Max Verstappen, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton all looking to strengthen their positions in the drivers' standings.

With no meaningful running completed in FP1, the second practice session now represents the first real opportunity for teams to evaluate their setups, gather tyre data and assess their long-run pace.

Will the weather finally allow the drivers to get some proper running under their belts, or could Las Vegas deliver another extraordinary session? Follow our liveblog below for all the latest updates from FP2.

articles.title: Dodgers Face Race Against Clock to Sign Japanese Phenom Shoki Oda
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers and teenage sensation Shoki Oda are facing a tight, complicated timeline to close a deal before the MLB lockout.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and teenage sensation Shoki Oda are facing a tight, complicated timeline to close a deal before the MLB lockout.

The Dodgers are in the race for Oda , who has met with 10 teams as nearly half the league is interested in him.

LA is the prohibitive favorite for Oda, but even if they secure a commitment, the timeline will be tricky.

How the lockout may impact the Shoki Oda pursuit

If the league wasn't facing a prolonged pause in action, the Dodgers' pursuit of Oda might be straightforward: wait until Jan 15, 2027, and offer him a massive amateur international free-agent bonus.

The current international amateur free agency window ends on Dec. 15, and the lockout starts on Dec. 1, leaving Oda and the Dodgers less than two weeks if LA can muster up a solid offer with their remaining bonus money.

If the Dodgers are out of bonus pool funds or low on them, Oda and the Dodgers may be waiting for either the money to kick in January or the new collective bargaining agreement to establish new rules for signing international amateurs.

During the last lockout, teams got their bonus pool money refreshed, which would be the best case for Oda.

However, international free agency could be overhauled.

According to Chunichi Sports, a Japanese news outlet , "Oda understands that he will not be able to sign a contract during the lockout period," the story read after translation.

For a player like Oda, if he wants to join a big-league team and avoid the Japanese NPB posting rules, he can either apply for amateur free agency or sign with a college and enter the amateur draft in a handful of years.

With modern NIL rules, Oda has a path to make a good deal of money in college, but he would be forced to stay for three years.

College seems unlikely, while a return to Japan, to the Yomiuri Giants where he was drafted, is still a long shot.

Given how definitive the signals are about his commitment to playing in America, he will need a major mindset shift.

For the Dodgers, the best they can hope for is a handshake agreement from Oda to sign for as much bonus money as reasonably possible, whether in January or down the line.

Anything short of that, and the rest of the teams lurking in the background will have a shot to nab him.

articles.title: Dolphins rookie WR still confident he'll show out despite slow start
articles.summary: The Dolphins took a receiver with first-round talent in the third round of this year's draft, and while he's had a slow start, he can still be great.
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins rookie wide receiver Chris Bell was having a great final season at Louisville, catching 72 passes for 917 yards and six touchdowns before he tore his ACL in a late-November matchup against SMU that the Cardinals lost 38-6.

Now, nearly a full year after the injury, Bell is battling another knee ailment that kept him out of the team's Week 10 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. However, he isn't concerned about it going forward.

"It was nothing that really hurt me," Bell told reporters on Thursday. "I'm good. It was just a little hyperextension, nothing too serious."

While he missed the offseason recovering from the torn ACL, the 22-year-old returned to the field in time for the season opener, but his NFL career has started slowly, catching just 12 passes for 148 yards in his eight games.

Things haven't gone the way he would like so far this year, but he feels that he'll still prove himself to be a reliable weapon in Miami's offense.

"I ain't going to lie," Bell said. "Nobody has seen the real Chris Bell yet.... "It takes time to get back from an ACL. I didn't know that until going through this journey. Before I came back, I was hoping to go back out there and ball. I've got to work my way back into who I am. I am slowly getting back to myself."

In four years at Louisville, Bell caught 151 passes for 2,166 yards and 12 touchdowns. If he can return to the player he was before the ACL injury, the Dolphins will have gotten a steal in the third round, but he needs to show he can be that guy at this level.

articles.title: Northern Kentucky cruises to 93-41 victory over D-III's Berea

articles.body:
HIGHLAND HEIGHTS, Ky. (AP) — Donovan Rakotonanahary scored 17 points as Northern Kentucky beat Division III's Berea 93-41 on Thursday night .

Rakotonanahary also had three steals for the Norse (3-3). B.J. Davis-Ray scored 16 points on 7-for-11 shooting with three steals. Noah Pagotto had 14 points and shot 3 of 5 from the field and 8 of 9 from the free-throw line.

Dominique Anthony led the Mountaineers with seven points.

Up next: Northern Kentucky hosts Georgia Southern in its next matchup on Monday.

articles.title: Strong start, familiar uncompetitive finish; Penguins lose 5-2
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins’ woes continued Thursday night at PPG Paints Arena.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Penguins ' woes continued Thursday night at PPG Paints Arena. Things started out well enough, and the Penguins even took a 1-0 lead, but the St. Louis Blues scored the next four goals on the way to a 5-2 win.

According to ESPN Research, 77% of teams in a playoff spot on American Thanksgiving since the NHL adopted its wild-card format in 2013-14 have gone on to make the postseason. With the holiday a week away, the Penguins (7-12-2) and Blues (11-9-2) came into Thursday's game in similar situations. Both teams entered the night outside the playoff picture with nearly identical recent form: the Penguins were 4-5-1 in their previous 10 games, while the Blues were 5-4-1. But only one of them looked like it had postseason aspirations.

The Penguins' new-look lines came out flying in the first period, playing with a speed that tilted the ice in their favor. They outshot the Blues 8-4, and Rickard Rakell accounted for five of those shots, including the one that put Pittsburgh up 1-0.

As good as the Penguins were in the first, they were just as bad in the second. They gave up three goals and were outshot by an astounding 22-10 margin in the frame.

articles.title: Fernando Alonso Calls Dakar Challenge ‘Another Level’
articles.summary: Fernando Alonso says the Dakar rally is harder than Formula 1. He details the mental strain and the unknown terrain he faces in 2027.
articles.body:
Fernando Alonso says the Dakar rally is a much harder test than Formula 1 racing. He told reporters that the unknown nature of the event makes it "another level" of difficulty. For a second time, the Spanish driver will return to the Dakar rally thanks to Aston Martin's three-car lineup. His return comes after he finished third in the 2020 event while driving for Toyota.

Alonso explained the mental gap between racing on a known track and racing in the wild. In Formula 1, drivers repeat the same thing lap after lap to perfect their driving style. The Dakar rally requires constant improvising because drivers do not know what happens next. He noted that the eyes cannot blink for four or five hours during the race. The focus on not blinking caused him headaches during his first test days.

The route for the 2027 Dakar will run from Portugal to Morocco. Originally scheduled for Saudi Arabia, the event was moved because of regional instability. The event's relocation to new conditions increases the difficulty for drivers. Alonso said "And Dakar is to the unknown; every metre is new" when discussing the challenge, according to Formula1.com . He feels the task is bigger for him because he did not grow up in that type of racing.

With the Dreadnought, Aston Martin will make its debut in the event. This is a real-world competition version of a car the manufacturer designed for the new game "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4." Alonso will have Marc Coma as his co-driver for the upcoming race.

Alonso knows he faces a steep climb to win the title. Sebastian Loeb, likely the greatest rally driver in history, is his teammate. Loeb has tried to win the Dakar nine or 10 times and has not achieved the win yet. Alonso said "I think I was competitive" when he reflected on his 2020 performance.

He admitted he had a good six months of preparation and thousands of kilometres of driving before that race. He does not have that same amount of time or distance in his current schedule. Despite the lack of prep, Alonso says the big challenge is what makes the event appealing. He wants to attempt to win it one day in the future.
